ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Clonus after an interaction

A 34-year-old woman taking sertraline begins tramadol after a dental procedure. Within a day she develops agitation, sweating, diarrhea and a temperature of 38.8 C. Examination shows brisk reflexes and inducible ankle clonus. Which diagnosis best explains the combined mental, autonomic and neuromuscular findings?

  1. Anticholinergic toxicity
  2. Opioid intoxication
  3. Uncomplicated panic attack
  4. Serotonin syndrome
  5. Neuroleptic malignant syndrome
Answer and explanation

Serotonin syndrome

The acute serotonergic drug combination and clonus strongly support serotonin toxicity.

Option explanations

Serotonin syndrome: The acute serotonergic drug combination and clonus strongly support serotonin toxicity.

Neuroleptic malignant syndrome: Dopamine blockade, marked generalized rigidity and a slower evolution would fit better.

Anticholinergic toxicity: Dry skin, urinary retention and reduced bowel activity are more typical than diaphoresis and diarrhea.

Opioid intoxication: Respiratory depression and reduced consciousness would be more typical.

Uncomplicated panic attack: Fever and objective clonus are not explained by a panic attack.
